definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.intro: Throughout these Terms of Service, when we say:
definitions.bitTasker: "BitTasker," "we," "us," or "our" refers to BitTasker, the company that develops and maintains the BitTasker platform.
definitions.services: "Services" refers to the features and functions provided by the BitTasker platform.
definitions.platform: "Platform" refers to our website, mobile applications, and other related services.
definitions.user: "User," "you," or "your" refers to individuals who use our platform in any capacity.
definitions.tasker: "Tasker," refers to users who post tasks requesting services.
definitions.taskee: "Taskee" refers to users who offer to perform services for Taskers.
definitions.task_contract: "Task Contract" refers to the agreement formed between a Tasker and a Taskee when an offer is accepted.
definitions.nostr: "Nostr" refers to the decentralized protocol that powers communications and identity on the BitTasker platform.
definitions.bitcoin: "Bitcoin" refers to the cryptocurrency used for payments on the BitTasker platform, including on-chain, Lightning Network, and Liquid Network transactions.
definitions.service_fee: "Service Fee" refers to the fee BitTasker charges for facilitating connections between Taskers and Taskees.

scope.title: 1. Scope of BitTasker Services
scope.point1: BitTasker provides a decentralized platform that enables Taskers to publish task requests and Taskees to make offers to complete these tasks.
scope.point2: The platform uses the Nostr protocol for identity, data storage, and communications, with Bitcoin and fiat as payment methods.
scope.point3: When a Tasker accepts a Taskee's offer, a Task Contract is created directly between these parties.
scope.point4: Upon task completion and confirmation, funds are released from the secure payment contract to the Taskee.
scope.point5: Both parties are encouraged to review and provide feedback after task completion, to help the community.

role.title: 2. BitTasker's Role and Obligations
role.point1: BitTasker provides the platform and technical infrastructure that enables the connection between Taskers and Taskees.
role.point2: BitTasker only permits individuals over 18 years of age to become Users.
role.point3: BitTasker may refuse service or suspend accounts of users who violate these terms.
role.point4a: BitTasker does not store your private keys or have access to your encrypted messages.
role.point4b: BitTasker cannot recover lost keys or passwords.
role.point4c: BitTasker does not have the ability to reverse, or intervene, in transactions.
role.point5: BitTasker accepts no liability for any aspect of the interaction between Taskers and Taskees, including but not limited to the description, performance, or delivery of services.
role.point6: BitTasker is not responsible for and does not warrant the truth or accuracy of any information provided by Users.
role.point7: The platform is provided "as is" and without any warranty or condition, express or implied.

ugc.title: 3a. User Generated Content, Objectionable Content & Moderation
ugc.intro: BitTasker is a platform where users post tasks, bids, messages, and profile information. We are committed to maintaining a safe and respectful environment. This section defines what constitutes objectionable content, how to report it, and how we act on reports.
ugc.objectionable_intro: The following types of content are strictly prohibited on BitTasker and constitute objectionable content:
ugc.objectionable1: Spam, unsolicited commercial messages, or repetitive content designed to manipulate search results or rankings.
ugc.objectionable2: Illegal content, including but not limited to content that facilitates illegal services, human trafficking, drug sales, weapons sales, or any activity prohibited by applicable law.
ugc.objectionable3: Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) or any content that sexually exploits or endangers children. BitTasker has zero tolerance for child sexual abuse and exploitation (CSAE). Any such content will be immediately removed from our relay, and the account will be permanently banned. We will report such content to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) and relevant law enforcement authorities as required by applicable law.
ugc.objectionable4: Profanity, hate speech, or content that promotes discrimination based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or national origin.
ugc.objectionable5: Nudity, sexually explicit content, or graphic violence not relevant to the services offered.
ugc.objectionable6: Impersonation of any person, company, or entity, including other BitTasker users.
ugc.objectionable7: Harassment, threats, intimidation, or bullying of any user.
ugc.objectionable8: Content that infringes on intellectual property rights, including copyrights and trademarks.
ugc.objectionable9: False, misleading, or deceptive content, including fake reviews or fraudulent task listings.
ugc.reporting_intro: BitTasker provides clearly labeled, readily accessible in-app tools to report objectionable content and block users. You can report:
ugc.reporting1: Any task listing — using the three-dot (⋮) menu on any task card.
ugc.reporting2: Any bid — using the three-dot (⋮) menu on any bid card.
ugc.reporting3: Any message — using the three-dot (⋮) menu on any message.
ugc.reporting4: Any user — using the three-dot (⋮) menu on any user profile.
ugc.reporting_types: When submitting a report, you must select a report category: Spam, Illegal content, Profanity or hateful speech, Nudity or explicit content, Impersonation, or Other (with a required description). Reports are broadcast as cryptographically signed events on the Nostr network and reviewed by BitTasker relay operators.
ugc.blocking_intro: You may block any user at any time using the three-dot (⋮) menu on their content or profile. Blocking a user:
ugc.blocking1: Immediately hides all of their content from your view, including tasks, bids, and messages.
ugc.blocking2: Updates your personal mute list, which is stored as a Nostr event (NIP-51 Kind 10000) on the relay.
ugc.blocking3: Can be undone at any time from the Muted Users section in your Settings.
ugc.action_intro: Reports are submitted as cryptographically signed Nostr events (NIP-56) and are visible to BitTasker relay operators. BitTasker will use best efforts to review reports on its own relay and take appropriate action within a reasonable timeframe. The scope of BitTasker's moderation is limited to what it technically controls, as described below.
ugc.action_sla_title: What BitTasker Can and Cannot Do
ugc.action_sla_intro: Because BitTasker is built on the decentralized Nostr protocol, its moderation capabilities are technically bounded:
ugc.action_sla1: BitTasker operates its own relay. Reports of violations will be reviewed on a best-efforts basis, with priority given to reports of illegal content, explicit content, and harassment.
ugc.action_sla2: Upon confirming a violation, BitTasker may ban the reported user from its relay. This prevents their content from appearing in the BitTasker client for all users.
ugc.action_sla3: BitTasker cannot remove content from third-party Nostr relays it does not operate. Content may remain accessible through other Nostr clients or relays outside BitTasker's control.
ugc.action_sla4: Users can immediately and independently hide any user's content using the in-app block/mute feature, without waiting for relay-level moderation.
ugc.action1: Users confirmed to have violated these Terms may be banned from the BitTasker relay, which prevents their content from appearing in the BitTasker client.
ugc.action2: Repeated or severe violations may result in a permanent ban from the BitTasker relay.
ugc.action3: BitTasker reserves the right to ban any user from its relay for content that violates these Terms, at its sole discretion.
ugc.decentralized_note: Important: Because BitTasker is built on the Nostr protocol, content is stored across a decentralized network of relays that BitTasker does not own or operate. BitTasker can only act on its own relay and cannot guarantee the removal of content from third-party relays outside of its control. Muting a user is a client-side action that immediately hides their content from your view regardless of which relay their content is stored on.

bitcoin.title: 4. Bitcoin Payments
bitcoin.point1: Users acknowledge that Bitcoin transactions are irreversible and BitTasker cannot recover funds sent to incorrect addresses.
bitcoin.point2: BitTasker uses smart contract-based secure payment contracts for task payments to provide security for both parties.
bitcoin.point3: When a Task Contract is created, the Tasker must deposit the agreed amount into the secure payment contract.
bitcoin.point4: Service Fees are deducted from the task payment when funds are released from the secure payment contract.
bitcoin.point5: Bitcoin price volatility: Both parties acknowledge that the value of Bitcoin can fluctuate and agree that once a price is set in Bitcoin for a task, it will not be adjusted due to price fluctuations.
bitcoin.point6: Users are responsible for any taxes or regulatory compliance related to their transactions.

fees.title: 5. Dynamic Fee Structure
fees.point1: BitTasker implements a level-based system that rewards active users with benefits.
fees.point2: Users can earn levels by successfully completing tasks (as Taskees) or hiring Taskees (as Taskers).
fees.point3: The service fee is the same for every asset, including Bitcoin and rBTC: 2.5%, 2.0%, or 1.5% per side, based on activity in the past 30 days. A repeat partnership is 1% per side. Higher levels may also include additional platform privileges. Bitcoin at launch, USDT coming soon.
fees.point4: The dynamic fee structure is designed to reward repeat business and active platform participation.
fees.point5: BitTasker reserves the right to modify the fee structure at any time.

encryption.title: 6. End-to-End Encryption and Privacy
encryption.point1: All direct messages between users are end-to-end encrypted.
encryption.point2: BitTasker cannot access the content of your private conversations.
encryption.point3: Users are responsible for maintaining the security of their private keys.
encryption.point4: If you lose access to your private keys, BitTasker cannot recover your encrypted messages or account.

language.title: 7. Multi-Language Support
language.point1: BitTasker offers automatic translation features to facilitate communication between users who speak different languages.
language.point2: While we strive for accuracy, users acknowledge that automatic translations may not be perfect and could sometimes lead to misunderstandings.
language.point3: In case of any discrepancy between different language versions of these Terms, the English version shall prevail.
language.point4: To avoid any confusion, it is recommended to be as clear as possible in communications.

disputes.title: 8. Dispute Resolution
disputes.point1: In the event of a dispute between a Tasker and a Taskee, both parties must attempt to resolve the issue directly through the platform's messaging system.
disputes.point2: If the parties cannot reach a resolution, our secure payment contract system will be used to resolve the dispute.
disputes.point3: Secure payment contracts are implemented with smart contracts on the Rootstock network where only the tasker and taskee control the funds.
disputes.point4: Since BitTasker does not have access to your funds, we are unable to intervene in the event that a tasker and taskee have a dispute.
